newsitem.title: USA: CME live, feeder cattle rally ahead of USDA data.
newsitem.headline: CME live, feeder cattle rally ahead of USDA data.

text.p: Evening of positions ahead of the USDA Cattle-on-Feed report accounted for the bulk of trade in both CME live and feeder cattle futures but prices rallied late as scattered buying touched off buy stops, traders said.

Live cattle closed 0.700 to 0.125 cent a lb higher with June up most at 65.175 cents and August up 0.550 at 64.275 cents. Feeder cattle ended up 1.050 to unchanged with August up most at 78.275 cents.

Reports of increased packer interest developing for cash cattle and expectations cash beef prices are near or at a bottom and will work higher, prompted much of the support in live cattle futures ahead of the report, traders said.
"Beef is at a level that has attracted very good retail interest," one trader said, referring to recent brisk wholesale-to-retail sales, albeit at lower prices.
Some technical buy stops were hit in August early and futures continued to drift up on the position squaring before the report, they added.

Analyst estimates on the report put June 1 total on-feed cattle supplies in the seven primary states at an average of 113.2 percent of a year ago in a range of 111.5 to 114 percent. A number at the high end would be a record high. May placement estimates averaged 117.2 in a range of 110.5 to 124 percent of a year earlier and May marketings averaged 99 in a range of 97 to 100.5 percent.

R.J. O'Brien and Refco bought June early while Rosenthal Collins sold, traders said. Refco, Rosenthal Collins and Smith Barney bought August. Lind-Waldock spread long August/short October with E.D.&F. Man on the other side. Local spreaders sold October. In live cattle options, commission house bought August 66 calls early and then turned sellers later, pit sources said.

Feeder cattle futures rallied sharply late as buy stops were triggered. Lack of sell orders early and scattered buying sparked by an oversold condition pushed futures up late into the buy stops. Some traders also look for firmer cash feeder markets ahead.
Expectations fed cattle prices could firm next week translated into optimism that demand for feeder cattle would increase, especially with feed costs expected to ease, they said.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was off $0.03 at $77.19 per cwt.
Cargill Investor Services bought August late while LIT division of First Options bought September, pit sources said.
